subject: Hybrid-mode SLA addendum: mapping time-to-first-token vs sustained token throughput
messages:
From: Helen Park <h.park@pulsehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: ops@pulsehealth.com
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA ask: streaming TTFT vs sustained tokens/sec expectations

Hi Marissa,

Quick one from our infra & compliance team. For our integration we need explicit language around streaming endpoints (time-to-first-token) vs non-streaming endpoints (complete-response latency) and the expected tokens/sec baseline for sustained workloads. Two specific asks:

1) Can Redwood commit a measured definition for "time-to-first-token" (how it is measured at the edge, measurement percentile and warm/cold start carveouts)?
2) For streaming endpoints we need a quantifiable tokens/sec expectation for sustained traffic (we plan to run 50 concurrent sessions during peak).

We also want to understand how fallback behavior (to a smaller quantized model or to a non-streaming response) affects SLA calculation and credits.

Can you send a single-page proposal that maps metrics to breach definitions and monitoring primitives? We can then route to procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Park
Director, Platform Ops
PulseHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Helen Park <h.park@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, soojin_lee@redwood.example
Date: 2026-06-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLA ask: streaming TTFT vs sustained tokens/sec expectations

Hi Helen — thanks, this is a good scope. Attached is a short addendum draft (pulse-proposed-sla-addendum-v1.pdf) and a measurement spreadsheet (measurement-definitions.xlsx) that map the metrics you asked for to how we instrument them in the Console. High-level summary below so you don't have to open attachments immediately.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Definition: "Time-to-first-token (TTFT)" = time from request arrival at the Redwood edge (ingress timestamp) to the first application token byte emitted on the streaming socket. Measured per-request, reported as P50/P95/P99.
- Baseline numeric targets (pilot): TTFT (streaming, small payloads <=64 tokens) P95 <= 220 ms, P99 <= 450 ms.
- Sustained emission: tokens/sec measured as a 30s sliding-window per-connection metric. Baseline sustained throughput target = >= 250 tokens/sec per concurrent stream for the stated model family under Dedicated capacity. We call out model/quantization variants as separate rows in the attachment.
- Non-streaming endpoints: full-response latency P95 <= 350 ms for responses <=512 tokens when not batched; batched endpoints have separate commit windows and are excluded from per-request TTFT.
- Fallback behavior: when we route to a compatible but smaller/quantized variant (auto-fallback), that connection is annotated and the request is excluded from TTFT SLO calculation for the first 60s of the fallback event; sustained tokens/sec is computed against the actual served model flavor so credits are only applied when the route is marked as "expected model" per the deployment config.
- Measurement & monitoring: SLOs use a 30-day rolling window, alerts at P95 breach for 24 hours. All token timestamps and edge arrival markers are exported to your Console route dashboard and to the request logs (token-level timestamps). We can provide synthetic test harness runs from us-west to reproduce.

Next steps: we propose a two-week pilot to run synthetic traffic and capture baseline numbers. Karthik (cc'd) will propose measurement semantics and weili in legal (Soojin, cc'd) will annotate carveouts/credits. If these targets look reasonable, we'll prepare a short amendment for procurement/DocuSign.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Helen Park <h.park@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLA ask: streaming TTFT vs sustained tokens/sec expectations — measurement semantics & caveats

Hi Helen — quick technical notes so the SLA language is unambiguous. I put more detail in measurement-definitions.xlsx but calling out the important bits here: 

Measurement semantics:
- TTFT start: timestamp when the HTTP/2 (or websocket) request is accepted by the edge LB and the request headers are parsed. End: first token bytes flushed to downstream socket (not the full application chunk). This excludes client-side receive delays.
- Percentiles: SLOs published as P50 / P95 / P99 over the configured evaluation window (30-day rolling). We recommend P95 for operational SLO and P99 for legal breach discussion.
- Cold starts: any request served by a model instance that has been idle for > 300s is annotated as a cold-start; cold-starts are excluded from SLOs for a 24h test running a 1-week ramp. After steady-state we include them.
- Sustained tokens/sec: computed per-connection using a 30s sliding median; for aggregated reporting we publish per-route median and the 10th percentile of per-connection sustained rates so you can size concurrency.

Fallback & model variants:
- Automatic fallback to quantized variants is opt-in per route. When on, Redwood tags the request with the actual served model id (model.flavor) and publishes both the original requested model and actual served model in the logs. SLO calculation can be configured: either 1) count all served requests against the original model SLO (stricter), or 2) compute SLOs per actual served flavor (recommended; avoids spurious breaches during capacity events).

Billing/credits tie-in:
- SLA credits are computed based on 1-minute buckets where aggregated P95 TTFT exceeds the committed threshold for > 60 continuous minutes. For streaming token-rate shortfalls, credits scale by the percentage delta between committed sustained rate and observed 30s sliding median across the affected buckets. Exact formula in the addendum appendix.

I'll be available to run the synthetic harnesses and share raw logs so PulseHealth can validate the token-level timestamps.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Helen Park <h.park@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLA ask: streaming TTFT vs sustained tokens/sec expectations — operational carveouts

Hi all — operational/legal points to note before we finalize:
- Force majeure & customer-induced load: If PulseHealth runs synthetic tests that cause congestion outside agreed windows and that congestion propagates into production, we will exclude those windows from breach computation if we provide prior notice and coordinate the runs.
- Measurement arbitration: for disputes we will share raw logs and run a joint re-evaluation using the measurement-definitions.xlsx; if still in disagreement an independent measurement snapshot (agreed SaaS tool) will be used.
- Credit caps and remedy: credits limited to a percentage of monthly invoice (see addendum appendix). For pilot phase we recommend monitoring-only (no credits) for 14 days, then move to full SLA when both sides are comfortable.

Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Ops & Compliance
Redwood Inference
